_about: Chapter 3's boss: the ghost of level 3-32 (level31b), decoded from android_game.bin,
ETHCallback_ghost (bytes 451999..457261) with its helpers in the same file.
It is the game's SECOND boss and shares nothing with the first. The beholder glides,
throws rolling stones, is hurt by a stone rising through it, fires rings of spikes and
raises a button when it dies. The ghost flies a waypoint path, shoots the player, is hurt
by FIRE, summons a minion when hurt, and drops a KEY when it dies. Boss.hpp is the
beholder's and stays that way; this is its own module for that reason.
FIVE states, not four, and their numbers are written into the callback's first six
instructions: APPEARING 0, SHOOTING 1, RAGE_MODE 2, DAMAGE 3, DEATH 4, and
GHOST_RADIUS 64. The init block writes hp 3, elapsedTime 0, state 0 and shotsFired 0.
HOW IT IS HURT, which is the whole reason this step follows the fire diamond. The
SHOOTING arm ends with isBurned(this): burned, it goes to DAMAGE, takes hp += -1, calls
healBurn(this) and plays playGhostDamageSound. Nothing else in the level can burn it, so
the fire diamond IS the weapon - the fireballs a converted portal shot becomes. A port
that built this boss without the fire diamond would have an invulnerable boss.
WHAT LEVEL31B IS. The level holds a keyhole (152, 204) and a door_locked (120, 160),
both metadata/color yellow, and NO KEY ANYWHERE. The only key in the level is the one
this boss drops when it dies. So the fight is the lock, and Keys is what opens it.
WHEN IT IS THERE (the owner's standing ruling R4, planning step 98): NOT from the level's
start. The level places ghost_pos, which is only where it flies to; the ghost.ent is added
by the black knight's own death (spawn below), wherever and however the knight dies, and
flies from there. Before it there is no ghost, no shot and no restock.
FOOTAGE (out/parity/footage/F15.md) disagrees with 'fire is the weapon' above: a fireball
passes through the ghost, a sensor, and only a barrel's explode() can burn it. The port
keeps the fireball, and says why in _not_built.

_note: The boss_spawn node, and it is NOT shaped like the beholder's. An adder carries
metadata/entity naming what to spawn ('beholder.ent'), and Boss::Plays reads that
field. ghost_pos carries no `entity` metadata at all - the NODE NAME is the whole of
it - so Ghost::Plays matches the entity name instead. Mirroring Boss::Plays literally
would return false for every level and leave level31b inert with no visible cause.
entity_roles.json files all four bosses under boss_spawn: adder (1-32), dragon.ent
(2-32), ghost_pos (3-32), dark_dragon_spawn (4-32) and dragon_knight_spawn. The role is
deliberately NOT in Roles::IsPorted; test_mp_start asks per NODE instead, so building
one boss never claims another. level31a's dragon stays inert and stays honest.

_source: THE OWNER'S STANDING RULING R4 (in favour of what the original does): the ghost appears after the
black knight dies. ETHCallback_ghost_minion (bytes 451487..451999, the remake's out/parity/asbc/
all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce; decode/D8.md section 2 and 4, D8_check.md): #1-6 currentPos =
GetPosition() before the minion's own callback runs; #25 ETHCallback_minion, whose only DeleteEntity
(#1478-1504) follows isDestroyed - a killer floor, a strike or a burn all end there; #35-40 once
!IsAlive(): #43-78 AddEntity('ghost.ent', currentPos + vector3(0, 0, scale(-1)), 0, out, '',
scale(0.3)); #92-94 playGhostAppearSound; #96-103 DeleteEntity(SeekEntity(1430)). 'ghost.ent' is
added nowhere else in the listing and placed by no scene (D8 section 4), and its callback is
ETHCallback_ghost by the engine's naming rule (ETHASUtil.cpp:63-68): the spawned entity IS the boss.
by_entity is the marker's entity the sim holds since R16 (minions.json spawn, planning step 97).
z_offset_units is scale(-1): one level unit behind its knight at any screen (00_order 8.13 K13).
scale is scale(0.3): the entity's scale at its init, which waypoint 0 reads back (appear below).
deletes_entity_id: level31b's entity 1430, anti_sight_wall.ent at (528, 192), a sensor with no
sprite; the converter names its node anti_sight_wall_ent_1430 (tscn.py _node_name). The port has
no minion sight, so taking it away changes nothing the port plays (planning step 98).
_first_callback: INFERRED, and pinned by test_mp_ghost: ghost.ent is static=1, so its callback is queued from a
visible bucket during the frame's draw and runs in the NEXT update (ETHScene.cpp:547-572,
ETHActiveEntityHandler.cpp:145-167; D8 section 4's side finding). So the tick the knight dies adds
the ghost at the .ent's own look (white, alpha 1) at scale 0.3, and its init block and first
APPEARING update run on the tick after.

_note: ETHCallback_ghost's init block (bytes 451999..457261 #26-324) builds a WaypointManager
(repeat false, raw SetV1 [10, 0] #102) of FIVE addWaypoint calls (#173-301), each Waypoint(pos,
time, FloatColor(uint), filter, scale) - its `angle` field is read back as a uniform SetScale
(#428-439). The APPEARING arm (#369-494) calls update, then getCurrentPoint, and writes the
point's pos (SetPositionXY), colour (SetColor rgb), scale and alpha; on isLastFrame it sets
SHOOTING, shotsFired 0 and elapsedTime seed_elapsed_ms.
WaypointManager::update (42421..42634) is FrameTimer::set(0, count - 1, waypoints[frame].time,
repeat) then setCurrentStride(waypoints[frame].time): the time is added, a changed first or last
resets to frame 0 with no time (the first update, since the constructor's own set leaves last 0),
else it steps at most ONE frame once the time reaches the stride. getCurrentPoint (41513..42094)
blends the current waypoint into the next (the current one again on the last frame) by the
CURRENT one's filter of getBias = min(stride, time) / max(stride, 1). defaultFilter(v) = v and
smoothEnd(v) = sin(v x PIb) (313837..313971). So legs of 1200, 2500 and 50 ms, a fourth of 0 that
lasts one callback, and the fifth waypoint terminal (D8 section 3, D8_check section 3).
at: 'spawn' is the ghost's own GetPositionXY at its init (#107-112), the knight's point; 'quarter'
is midPoint = currentPos + (ghost_pos - currentPos) / 4 (#130-148), mid_fraction; 'anchor' is
ghost_pos (#114-128). argb is the FloatColor(uint) constant, a = (c >> 24) / 255 and so on
(86246..86521; the one-argument overload is DECODED, D8_check C6). scale 'spawn' is GetScale().x,
the spawn's scale(0.3).
FOOTAGE (out/parity/footage/F15.md section 3, r1 with the camera still): the path within 2-5 u of
this model from P0 = the knight's spot, the scale within 0.03, the black-to-grey change riding the
second leg with alpha 0.8 -> 1.
_seeds_note: On WaypointManager::isLastFrame the arm sets state SHOOTING, shotsFired 0 and
elapsedTime 3000 - NOT zero. Seeding the clock at the shot interval means the first
shot comes on the first frame of SHOOTING rather than three seconds later.

_source: What ETHCallback_ghost writes on the entity outside APPEARING (D8, system_5.md 5c-4 corrected by
D8): SHOOTING #510-512 SetFrame(0); RAGE_MODE #992-998 SetFrame(3) and SetAlpha(0.5), and #1199-1201
SetAlpha(1) as it goes back to SHOOTING; DAMAGE #789-816 SetAlpha(0.5) and bounce(this, V2_ONE,
vector2(1.1, 1.1), 500); DEATH #1220-1263 SetAlpha(1) and bounce(this, vector2(1.1, 1.1),
vector2(1.25, 1.25), 400). Nothing else writes the colour after APPEARING, the frame outside
SHOOTING and RAGE_MODE, or the scale outside APPEARING and the two bounces: each persists, so RAGE
shows the scale DAMAGE's bounce last left. bounce (utilEntityEffect bytes 327057..327527) keeps ONE
clock, blinkElapsedTime, made at 0 on its first call and never reset, advanced only by its own calls
(#27-39) before it reads it: the count of strides says which way it runs and smoothEnd of the
remainder where (Art::Pulse, the beholder's). ghost.png is 4 x 1 (ghost.ent SpriteCut): cell 3 is
the raging face.

_note: Every interval it seeks dark_mage.ent - the PLAYER - and fires only when the player's
x is past the x of the level's red_line entity. level31b puts red_line at (262, 110),
so the boss does not shoot at a player still on the left of the arena.
It also restocks the player's tools on that same beat, with addEntityIfItCantBeFound:
a barrel_bomb at barrel_spawn and a fire_diamond.ent at fire_diamond_spawn. That is
why level31b places both spawn markers, and why dropping the fire diamond down the
gutter mouth is survivable - the boss hands you another.
addEnemyShoot and ETHCallback_enemy_shoot are in ETHCallback_minion.angelscript, and
minions.json's _shooting_not_built already decoded them: enemy_shoot.ent carries
direction, destiny, casterPos, targetName and targetID, moves 120 units a second, and
kills with fakeRadius = scale(16) - an isCharacter target within that has hp set to 0.
killPortal is NOT reachable from this boss. That branch fires only when the shot's
target is named portal.ent, and the ghost always passes the player as its target. So
the step minions.json deferred stays deferred, and this shot only kills the player.
_nudge_px: ETHCallback_enemy_shoot (bytes 435266..436701) #1-56, on its first call: initialPos = GetPositionXY()
(the muzzle, casterPos), then AddToPositionXY(scale(direction x 16)) - the shot is moved 16 units
along its way before it first flies - and squaredDistance = |destiny - initialPos|^2 is its range,
measured from the muzzle and not from where the nudge left it (#75-108); #164-200 destroy once
|position - initialPos|^2 passes it. So the shot starts 16 units out and flies 16 units less.
Read since planning step 98 (the visuals plan's 12.2): a GAMEPLAY change - a shot now reaches the
player's point 16 / 120 s sooner than the port's did, and is drawn where the original draws it.
_cells: #126-137: SetFrame(_projectileFrameTimer.set(0, 5, 30, true)) every call - the ONE script-global
FrameTimer the player's shot steps too (art.json shot.animation), so every live shot's callback
adds its frame's time to it. enemy_shoot.ent: projectile_transparent.png, SpriteCut 6 x 1.
_pictures: What the calls add around it (effects.json, planning step 98): addEnemyShoot #127-168 portal_mark.ent
at vector3(finalPos, scale(32)); #62-71 projectile_shoot.ent at the nudged shot's own vector3; and
once destroyed, #324-363 startEarthquake(10) (not built on this track), portal_fail_in_antiportal.ent
at vector3(the shot's own point, 0) and playEnemyShootExplodeSound (not built).

_note: hp <= 0 goes straight to DEATH. Otherwise it holds at alpha 0.5, bounces (look), scatters
explosions, and after 4000 ms goes to RAGE_MODE rather than back to SHOOTING. It does not
hover: linearMotion is called only in SHOOTING and RAGE_MODE (#508, #990), and bounce writes
no position (#102 SetScale), so DAMAGE and DEATH hold it where the swing left it.
RAGE_MODE waits on its escort. While no minion.ent exists it spawns one - inside the
first 200 ms of the state - at the position of the level's minion_spawn_point, on the
wayA prefix, via spawnMinion. Once one exists it STAYS in rage until that minion is
gone; then the 200 ms window has passed and it returns to SHOOTING at alpha 1.
minion_spawn_point is NOT a minion_spawn marker and carries no role at all, which is
why Minions::Find never sees it and why this module resolves it by name. level31b puts
it at (436, 96); the wayA prefix resolves wayA0 (314, 208) hold 1000 and wayA1
(412, 208) hold 4000, which minions.json calls 'unclaimed' and assigns to this boss.
DEATH stops the boss music, bounces at 1.25 over 400 ms, scatters explosions, and at
3550 ms calls explode(pos, 2.0, 0), adds key.ent at its own position and deletes
itself.
The key's colour is NOT taken from level31b. key.ent's own CustomData holds exactly one
variable - a string named color with the value yellow - so every key.ent the game ever
adds is yellow by the entity's default, and level31b's keyhole and door being yellow is
the level agreeing with the entity rather than the source of the value.
blast_scale is recorded and NOT applied: explode's own radius is fire.json's blast_px,
and what the 2.0 multiplies is not established. The port drops the key and does not
blast, which is the conservative reading - a blast that killed the player at the moment
of victory would be a worse error than a missing one.

_not_built: DAMAGE and DEATH both scatter small_explosion_no_light.ent through overTimeEntityAdder
at 400 ms, at an offset of scale(64) * (0.4 + randF(0.7)) along a random angle, built
as (-cos, sin). Presentation, and random - recorded, not built.
The noise: all five ghost sounds, the appear sound among them (ETHCallback_ghost_minion #92-94).
playGameMusic(bossFight = true) IS built (the layer's updateMusic, from the ghost's init, #320-324;
DEATH's StopSample #1224-1243 leaves the level silent). level31b's no_music (Game::readProperties
#166-181), which leaves the level silent until then, is not: the port honours no level's no_music.
The scattered explosions (DAMAGE and DEATH's overTimeEntityAdder) and the death blast's 2.0.
The barrel bomb restock. addEntityIfItCantBeFound would put a barrel_bomb at
barrel_spawn; Fire owns bombs and fills them from the scene, so a mid-run bomb is the
same mid-run-Add step minions.json names for Fire::Burnable and Demolish::Breakable.
The FIRE DIAMOND restock IS built, because Diamonds holds its diamonds in a plain
vector and a diamond is not a body. RAGE_MODE's own restock of the fire diamond every frame
while the player lives (#1034-1071) is not built.
The body. ghost.ent is a static sensor, 128 x 139 at (5, -7): the original's portal ray has no
ghost.ent in its ignore list, so a shot across the box fails (F15 finding 2), and a fireball
passes through it, since ETHBeginContactCallback_fireball returns on a sensor (F15 finding 1) - so
in the original only explode() can burn the ghost. The port keeps its fireball test (Game.cpp:
a fireball within radius_px burns it), because the barrel that is the original's weapon is not
restocked here: explode-only would leave the port's ghost unkillable. The owner's to rule.
Static bucket clocks: ghost.ent's callback runs only while its bucket is on screen
(ETHScene.cpp:541-574); the port's runs every tick.
